clue.text: Moored vessel, and eminent people with it

parts.note: leading lights are people of eminence, so lights here means notable figures
hip and with it both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A boat at anchor shares its deck with celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightship is anchored permanently in place to serve as a floating lighthouse.

clue.text: Restricted number belonging to particular area?

definitions.text: Restricted number belonging to particular area?

parts.words: Restricted number belonging to particular area?
parts.note: read number as something that numbs: an anaesthetic whose effect is confined to one part of the body, and also something belonging to a neighbourhood

explanation.surface: A limited telephone number serving one district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a figure but is a thing that numbs, i.e. an anaesthetic acting only on one area.
explanation.definitionFit: A local anaesthetic numbs only one region, and the word also means belonging to a neighbourhood.

clue.text: Novel left where orchestral oboists sit

parts.note: gone means departed, having left
oboes belong to the woodwind section, so oboists sit with the wind players

explanation.surface: A book abandoned in the woodwind section of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell's famous 1936 book about the American Civil War is a novel.

clue.text: A ruse developed in attempt to secure funds

indicators.note: the attempt holds the shuffled letters fast inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: the letters develop into a new form, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A scheme is hatched to try to get hold of some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' makes EASUR from A RUSE, which 'to secure' places inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasury is a store of money, so it stands for funds.

clue.text: English novelist's combination of expectation and desire

definitions.meaning: Anthony ... wrote The Prisoner of Zenda
to want something while expecting it may happen

explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Hope was the English author of The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries define hope as a feeling of expectation and desire for something to happen.

clue.text: Containing pledge for girl on Circle Line?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for
a miss is a girl
a circle is shaped like the letter O
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A young woman travelling on a London Underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it splits into O and RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A promissory note contains a written pledge to pay, so the adjective describes something embodying a promise.

clue.text: Stand-in senior officer rejected with hesitation …

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the officer's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: COL is short for colonel, a senior army officer
um is the sound of a pause in speech

explanation.surface: A substitute colonel is turned down after some hemming and hawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns COL into LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric who temporarily covers for another, a stand-in.

clue.text: King leaves without braid on uniform

indicators.note: the king departs from the word, so his letter is taken out

parts.note: lacking means without
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch departs without the gold trimming on his uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' takes the K out of LACKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacing is ornamental braid or cord sewn onto military dress.

clue.text: Motion opposing bar music, partly?

parts.note: a counter is the bar in a shop or pub
a movement is one part of a symphony or other musical work

explanation.surface: A pub's music being only part of a larger piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A countermovement is a motion or campaign set up in opposition to another.

clue.text: Poor old man with teeth decayed

indicators.note: decay breaks things down, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly man whose teeth have rotted away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decayed' rearranges O, MAN and TEETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten means shabby and worn out, hence poor in quality.

clue.text: … despite once being involved in action?

definitions.text: … despite once being involved in action?

parts.words: despite once being involved in action?
parts.note: despite once meant scorn, and a legal action is heard in a court, so this is scorn shown within legal proceedings

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a locum hesitates even though once part of the action.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 6 Across for the surface only. Despite is an old word for scorn, and an action is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is the offence of showing disrespect to a court during legal proceedings.

clue.text: Most vulgar — frequently thrown out of Suffolk resort

indicators.note: the word for frequently is ejected from the resort's name

parts.note: Lowestoft is a seaside town in Suffolk, eastern England
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: The coarsest people are regularly expelled from a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowestoft is a seaside resort in Suffolk, England; 'thrown out of' removes OFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowest can mean most base or coarse, hence most vulgar.

clue.text: Sketch given out to test examinees, initially

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their normal order
initially takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An outline handed out as a test for exam candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges GIVEN to VIGNE; 'initially' gives TTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vignette is a brief descriptive piece of writing, a short sketch.

clue.text: Origin of article written in area of France

indicators.note: the article is written inside the name of the region

parts.note: Provence is a region of southern France
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Where an article published in a French region came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Provenance is the place of origin or history of ownership of something.

clue.text: Changing leader, explain endlessly about one's project

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the next piece
endlessly cuts off the last letter
the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: to interpret is to explain
I is one, and the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Someone tries to describe their venture but keeps changing the opening and never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing leader' swaps the opening I for E, giving ENTERPRET; 'endlessly' then drops its final T before the rest goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is an undertaking or venture, the same as a project.

clue.text: River increases in level, trapping many trains

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: the rising word traps the letter inside it

parts.note: rises means goes up
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

explanation.surface: A river swells and catches a large number of railway trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trapping' puts C (Roman 100, a common crossword 'many') inside RISES. 'Trains' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise someone is to drill or train them, so the verb form matches trains.

clue.text: Husband finally abandons faith, becoming communist

indicators.note: the husband's letter leaves from the very end of the word

parts.note: troth is an old word for faith or loyalty, as in plighting one's troth

explanation.surface: A husband eventually gives up his religion and turns to communism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally abandons' takes the last letter, H, off TROTH. Trot is short for Trotskyist.
explanation.definitionFit: Trot is informal shorthand for a Trotskyist, a type of left-wing radical.

clue.text: Twisted shop girl reportedly supplies poisonous gas

indicators.note: twisting distorts the word's letters into another order
reportedly means what is heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A bent shopgirl, people say, is handing out a toxic gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' turns SHOP into PHOS; 'reportedly' turns the name Jean into GENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosgene is a highly toxic gas used as a chemical weapon in the First World War.

clue.text: Provisions some purchase at supermarkets

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Food that some people buy at supermarkets.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, and provisions are supplies of food.

clue.text: Defeated after part of game is rigged, perhaps

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
a thrown match is one deliberately lost, an example of rigging

explanation.surface: A team is beaten after a portion of the match is fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six deliveries in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Overthrown means toppled or defeated, as a government might be.

clue.text: For example, Danish meat

definitions.meaning: Danish is an example of a language

explanation.walkthrough: Danish looks like a pastry beside the meat, but it is the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language such as Danish and is also a cut of meat.

clue.text: It's used for upholstery acceptable in revamped centre

indicators.note: the acceptable piece goes inside the reworked letters
revamping remakes the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: on means acceptable, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: Something fit for covering sofas at a refurbished centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revamped' gives CRETNE, which 'in' then opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cretonne is a heavy printed cotton fabric used for chair covers and curtains.

clue.text: Son meets church worker about rise

indicators.note: the worker goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a worker ant, the stock crossword worker
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A son meets a church employee concerning a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb or upward slope, a rise.

clue.text: Drink with strange youth leader after time

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the time abbreviation

parts.note: odd means strange

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink with an odd young chief once the hour comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' gives the first letter of 'youth', Y; 'after time' puts ODDY after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot drink of spirits with sugar and water.

clue.text: Leading church abandons formality

indicators.note: the church leaves the word, so its letters are removed

parts.note: starch means stiff formality of manner

explanation.surface: A prominent church gives up its stiff ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandons' removes CH from STARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Star as an adjective means principal or most prominent, i.e. leading.

clue.text: Malingering, as boxer's escort may be?

definitions.meaning: shirking work by pretending to be ill
someone walking a boxer dog may swing its leash about

explanation.walkthrough: A boxer here is a breed of dog, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pretending to be ill to avoid work, which is malingering.

clue.text: Plant uses sulphur, gaining slight advantage

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
an edge is a slight advantage over a rival

explanation.surface: A plant uses sulphur to gain a small advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant growing in wet ground.

clue.text: New style a composer adopted with serious intent

indicators.note: the reworked letters take in the composer
new suggests the word is made over, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Thomas Arne was an English composer, writer of Rule, Britannia

explanation.surface: A composer took up a fresh style with real purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' gives ESTLY, which 'adopted' opens just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means in a sincere, serious manner, with serious intent.
